Not checked because an earlier check failed.
Allow root access if your device asks. This may take up to 90 seconds.
LLCast cannot start on this device yet.
The receiver could not start. Restart LLCast to check again.
The check could not finish. Close LLCast and try again.
Allow LLCast in your root manager. Root access through ADB alone is not enough.
No root approval arrived in 90 seconds. Allow LLCast in your root manager, then reopen it.
The native receiver cannot load its decoder.
START LLCAST ON YOUR PC OR MAC
BACK POWER OR VOLUME RETURNS TO ANDROID
SCREEN RUNS AT %1$s HZ. 60 HZ IS SMOOTHEST
Send this screen, or show another one here.
Choose a mode to start receiving.
This screen runs at %1$s Hz. Motion is smoothest at 60 Hz, which you can set in Android’s display settings.
Connect this device to Wi-Fi or Ethernet first.
Hardware video decoding, or AV1 with dav1d. No root.
Direct display on supported rooted devices. AV1 with dav1d, or HEVC with Rockchip MPP. Back, Power or Volume returns to Android.
Requires 64-bit ARM Android, root access and a compatible direct display driver.
Type it as the receiver shows it while it waits. If it shows a port, as in 192.168.1.50:47801, include it.
Use an even width and height from 160 to 7680, and a frame rate from 1 to 240 fps.
Type a number of Mbps from 0.5 to 200, or choose Auto.
Checking this device and the receiver…
Reception: %1$s · %2$d fps · %3$.1f%% packets received · %4$d too late · %5$.1f%% frames corrupt
Packets are being lost: try a bandwidth budget of %1$s Mbps, or a lower profile.
Some packets arrive too late to use, usually from busy or weak Wi-Fi: try a bandwidth budget of %1$s Mbps, or move closer to the access point.
The receiver can’t decode this fast: it shows %1$d of %2$d fps. Try a lower profile, or a codec it decodes in hardware.
The receiver couldn’t decode some frames although no packets were lost: try another codec.
This device sends only %1$d of %2$d fps: it can’t capture and encode this fast. Try a lower profile.
" · capture to display: min %1$d ms, median %2$d ms"
" · capture to display: min %1$d ms, estimated median %2$d ms"
Screen capture wasn’t allowed. Press Start to ask again.
This device can’t encode video in hardware
Sending needs hardware HEVC or H.264 encoding at %1$s. Try a lower profile, or another device.
Choose Low, or reduce the resolution or frame rate under Custom.
Nothing answered at %1$s, port %2$d. Check that the receiver shows the LLCast waiting screen, that the address and port match, and that both are on the same network.
The receiver is on, but LLCast isn’t receiving
The device at %1$s answered, but LLCast isn’t running on it. Start LLCast there; it then shows its address.
Nothing could be sent to %1$s. Check the address, and that both devices are on the same network.
No device called “%1$s” was found. Type the numeric address the receiver shows, for example 192.168.1.50.
The receiver can’t decode this device’s video
This device encodes %1$s; the receiver decodes %2$s. Auto uses HEVC or H.264; choose AV1 under Codec if both have it.
This device can’t encode %1$s in hardware
It encodes %1$s. Choose Auto or one of those under Codec.
It decodes %1$s. Choose Auto or one of those under Codec.
The encoder or the network stopped. Press Start to try again.
The receiver can no longer decode %1$s
Another receiver may have taken its address. Press Start to check again.
Type the address the receiver shows while it waits, for example 192.168.1.50.
The address has an invalid port
Type the address as the receiver shows it, for example 192.168.1.50 or 192.168.1.50:47801. A port is a number from 1 to 65535.
This device can’t decode video in hardware
Normal mode needs hardware HEVC, H.264 or AV1 decoding, which nearly every Android device has. Try another device.
This device isn’t on a network
Connect it to Wi-Fi or Ethernet, then try again.
Another receiver may be running on this device. Close it, then try again.
Check that this device is connected to the network, then try again.
Open Receive again. If it keeps happening, this device’s decoder may not handle the stream.
Port %1$d is busy on this device, so LLCast uses port %2$d. If the sender has no Port box, add “:%2$d” to the address.
This sender uses %1$s, which this device can’t decode.
